title: What Carbon Nanotube Processors Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Carbon nanotube processors build CPUs from carbon nanotube transistors instead of silicon: semiconducting nanotubes switch faster with less energy, and their tiny size promises continued scaling. A complete working microprocessor (RV16X-NANO) has already run real programs on CNT technology. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Carbon Nanotube Processors: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Carbon Nanotube Processors in one line: Carbon nanotube processors build CPUs from carbon nanotube transistors instead of silicon: semiconducting nanotubes switch faster with less energy, and their tiny size promises continued scaling.
Why it matters: Nanotubes conduct electrons ballistically — they could extend Moore's law past silicon's limits while cutting energy per operation..
Where it is used: ultra-efficient processors, flexible electronics, 3D-stacked logic, radiation-hard space chips..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Carbon Nanotube Processors
title: Current Research State of Carbon Nanotube Processors
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Stanford/MIT teams built a 16-bit CNT microprocessor running real code, and later 3D CNT-CMOS integration.
